_format: concept: [what it is, what tradition reads into it, an example]

new_moon.what: The moon sits between Earth and Sun, its lit side facing away: a dark sky.
new_moon.meaning: A time to set intentions and begin quietly.
new_moon.example: New moon in Scorpio: begin something you've kept secret, even from yourself.

waxing_crescent.what: A thin growing sliver in the evening sky.
waxing_crescent.example: Send the first message about the job you want.

first_quarter.what: Half the moon is lit and growing.
first_quarter.example: If the plan wobbles this week, that's the first-quarter test.

waxing_gibbous.what: More than half lit, still growing.

full_moon.what: The moon is opposite the Sun, fully lit all night.
full_moon.meaning: Culmination, emotions high, what was hidden is revealed; a time to release.
full_moon.example: Full moon in Cancer: feelings about home come to the surface.

waning_gibbous.what: Past full, shrinking, rising later each night.
waning_gibbous.meaning: Gratitude and sharing what you learned.
waning_gibbous.example: Tell someone what this month taught you.

last_quarter.example: Delete, donate, close the tab you keep open.

waning_crescent.meaning: Rest and surrender before the next cycle.
waning_crescent.example: Sleep early; don't start anything big yet.

supermoon.what: A full or new moon close to perigee, the moon's nearest point to Earth: up to ~14% larger and ~30% brighter than at its farthest.
supermoon.meaning: Tradition reads it as the same moon, turned up.
supermoon.example: A super full moon: release with extra force.

blue_moon.what: The second full moon in one calendar month; it happens about every two and a half years.
blue_moon.meaning: A rare extra chance: 'once in a blue moon'.
blue_moon.example: Use it for something you've postponed for years.

lunar_eclipse.what: Earth's shadow falls on the full moon, turning it copper-red when total.
lunar_eclipse.meaning: Read in many traditions as a powerful ending or revelation.
lunar_eclipse.example: Something hidden shows its true colour.

solar_eclipse.what: The new moon passes in front of the Sun, somewhere on Earth.
solar_eclipse.meaning: A new beginning that arrives with a shock.
solar_eclipse.example: A door you didn't expect opens.

spring_tide.what: Around new and full moon, Sun and Moon pull in line: the year's higher high tides and lower low tides, usually peaking a day or two later. 'Spring' means 'springing up', not the season.
spring_tide.example: Emotions run high this week; name them before acting on them.

neap_tide.what: Around the quarter moons, Sun and Moon pull at right angles: the gentlest tides.
neap_tide.example: A quiet week for reflection rather than big moves.

king_tide.what: A spring tide when the moon is also near perigee: the highest tides of the year.
king_tide.example: If something has been building, it may crest now.

retrograde.what: From Earth, a planet seems to move backward against the stars for a few weeks; it's an effect of Earth overtaking it (or it overtaking Earth), not real backward motion.
retrograde.meaning: Tradition: review, revisit, re-do (Mercury: messages and travel; Venus: love and values).
retrograde.example: Mercury retrograde: reread before you send.

solstice.what: The Sun reaches its farthest north or south: the longest day in one hemisphere and the longest night in the other.
solstice.meaning: A turning point between light and dark.
solstice.example: What in your life is at its brightest, and what at its darkest?

equinox.what: The Sun crosses the equator; day and night are nearly equal everywhere.
equinox.example: What's out of balance this week?

cross_quarter.what: The midpoint between a solstice and an equinox; the old Celtic festivals (Imbolc, Beltane, Lammas, Samhain) sit near them.
cross_quarter.example: Mark the halfway point of the season.

weather_rain.meaning: Water: feelings, cleansing, letting things flow.
weather_rain.example: Rain on a Five of Cups day: let the grief rinse through.

weather_storm.meaning: Fire and air together: sudden insight, things shaken loose.
weather_storm.example: A storm and The Tower on the same day: let the false structure fall.

weather_clear.what: Clear sky where the user is.
weather_clear.example: A clear day for a clear decision.

weather_cloud.meaning: Air and the veiled: things not fully visible yet.
weather_cloud.example: Don't force an answer under clouds; ask again tomorrow.

weather_fog.meaning: The moon's realm: mystery, intuition over sight.
weather_fog.example: Trust what you feel more than what you see today.

weather_snow.meaning: Earth and stillness: rest, quiet, covering.
weather_snow.example: A day to pause plans and keep warm.

weather_wind.example: Expect news; let go of what the wind wants to take.

weather_heat.example: Act boldly, but count to ten.

history_reading.what: A playful reading of a historical moment: the real sky at that moment, and a card the deck gives that event (the same for everyone).
history_reading.meaning: Not a claim that the stars caused history; a way to play with symbols.
history_reading.example: The Moon landing happened under a waxing crescent moon: the 'first steps' phase.
